text:
maya: Noticing a UX quirk in the Go SDK generator stream. When I cancel the context mid-stream the client often waits until the server finishes the current write batch (~150ms) before Recv() returns. JS and Python clients return immediately. Thoughts?

daniel: Is the SDK using http.Transport without tying the request to ctx? If so, Cancel won't interrupt the socket read immediately on some platforms (esp http2).

maya: We are on net/http with default transport and http2 enabled. Also auth refresh is in play (token auto-refresh).

rachel: A concrete repro would help. Also curious if the generator stream exposes any Close/Abort API on the stream object? In our other SDKs we have stream.Close() that triggers a fast shutdown.

maya: Current usage in sampleapp:```go
ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 3*time.Second)
defer cancel()
stream, err := client.GeneratorStream(ctx, req)
if err != nil { log.Fatal(err) }
for {
  tok, err := stream.Recv()
  if err != nil { if err==io.EOF { break } ; log.Println("recv err", err); break }
  fmt.Print(tok.Text)
}
```
No explicit Close() call on stream in samples.

simon: That pattern assumes Recv will be interruptible by ctx. On some Go readers you need to call resp.Body.Close() or cancel the transport to break a blocking Read. If the SDK doesn't call NewRequestWithContext, cancel won't propagate.

daniel: Another angle: the runtime may flush an in-memory buffer of generated tokens in a single syscall once a batch is ready. If cancel happens while the runtime is mid-batch it may choose to finish the syscall. That leads to the 100-200ms window.\

maya: Right. The surprising thing is parity: JS/Python return quickly. So either our Go path is missing a context binding or the Go runtime uses a different wire behavior.

rachel: If we want a low-friction DX fix, options: (A) expose stream.Abort() on the Go SDK that closes underlying resp.Body and returns a context.Canceled to the caller; (B) ensure GeneratorStream uses http.NewRequestWithContext so net/http cancels reads; (C) add a RecvWithContext(ctx) helper.

simon: (A) is simplest for immediate remediation. (B) is ideally correct for parity. (C) is nice API sugar for downstream ergonomics. We should implement (B) + (A) as fallback.

daniel: Also add an integration test: fake runtime that writes chunks with a 200ms sleep between frames; client calls cancel after first frame and we assert Recv returns context.Canceled within e.g. 50ms. That will fail today and prove regression.

maya: I'll attach a small sampleapp change for onboarding that shows proper pattern including deferred stream.Close(); and an example of wrapping the resp.Body with ctx-aware reader if people are manually doing net/http.

rachel: One implementation note: when you Close resp.Body while another goroutine is Read-ing, Read returns immediately with error. That gives us deterministic interrupt. The SDK stream.Close should call resp.Body.Close and set a flag so subsequent Recv returns a clean error.

simon: Edge case: if auth refresh triggers a 401 midstream, the token refresh path might create a new request under the hood. We must ensure that any replacement request also uses the parent ctx. Otherwise canceling the original ctx won't cancel the follow-up request.

daniel: Good catch. Add to the checklist: "token refresher must call NewRequestWithContext(parentCtx, ...) when performing retry/refresh flows".

maya: File created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-go/issues/629 - "go: generator Recv latency after ctx cancel (http2 chunk flush)". I'll add repro, sampleapp diff, and suggested patch for stream.Close + request WithContext.

rachel: Small docs addition request: under Go SDK streaming docs include a section "Cancel & cleanup patterns" with code showing: 1) pass ctx into GeneratorStream; 2) call stream.Close() on error or cancel; 3) prefer using the provided sampleapp helper that drains and closes on early exit.

simon: Also update the quickstart sample to show defer stream.Close() right after getting the stream so folks don't forget. That avoids goroutine leaks when users bail early.

daniel: I'll add the e2e test to go-sdk/integration and tag runtime folks for a perf check on chunk buffering behavior.

dev-bot: Created issue #629: "go: generator Recv latency after ctx cancel (http2 chunk flush)" and linked PR #827 (sampleapp onboarding + stream.Close shim). Assigned to @maya and @daniel.

maya: Thanks everyone. Quick follow-up: should we bump the SDK minor version after this fix and call out the change in release notes as "stream cancellation parity and new stream.Abort()"?
rachel: Yes, this is a UX-affecting bug so include in the next minor with migration notes.
maya: Awesome. Closing this thread; will ping when PR is ready.
